items.title: Fake news game confers psychological resistance against online misinformation

judge.evidence_empirical: We conducted a large-scale evaluation of the game with N = 15,000 participants in a pre-post gameplay design.
judge.evidence_topic: we designed a psychological intervention in the form of an online browser game.
judge.reason: The abstract describes an online browser game (Bad News) that teaches about misinformation techniques, with an evaluation using15,000 participants in a pre-post design, and finds improved ability to spot and resist misinformation irrespective of demographic factors, directly matching the extracted data.

items.title: Prebunking interventions based on the psychological theory of “inoculation” can reduce susceptibility to misinformation across cultures

judge.evidence_empirical: "the online “fake news” game, Bad News, can confer psychological resistance against common online misinformation strategies (e.g., conspiracy theories, manipulating emotions, political polarization) across different cultures"
judge.evidence_topic: "the online “fake news” game, Bad News, can confer psychological resistance against common online misinformation strategies (e.g., conspiracy theories, manipulating emotions, political polarization) across different cultures"
judge.reason: O resumo não descreve o delineamento experimental nem mídidas pré e pós-jogo, embor a estudo relte achados empíricos. O mídodo informado (experimentos in-game com pré e pós) nã é suportado pelo resumo.

items.title: Game-based inoculation versus graphic-based inoculation to combat misinformation: a randomized controlled trial

judge.evidence_empirical: Abstract: 'A total of 180 Chinese participants were randomly assigned to game-based inoculation, graphic-based inoculation, and control groups.'
judge.evidence_topic: Abstract: 'this study employed inoculation theory and developed an interactive game to help the public counter misinformation.' and '180 Chinese participants.' No mention of COVID-19, vaccines, elections, or partisan politics.
judge.reason: O artigo é sobre um jogo de inoculação contra desinformação com participantes chineses, sem tópicos excluídos (COVID-19, vacinas, eleições, política partidária); é um estudo empírico com dados próprios (ensaio controlado randomizado); o tipo de estudo e método extraídos (ECR, três grupos, acompanhamento de 2 semanas) conferem com o resumo; o achado principal é plenamente sustentado pelo resumo (redução da credibilidade e intenção de partilha, jogo mais eficaz que gráfico na credibilidade, efeito estável após 2 semanas).

items.title: Gamified Inoculation Against Misinformation in India: A Randomized Control Trial

judge.evidence_empirical: We report the results of a game-based intervention against misinformation in India. The game is based on the mechanism of psychological inoculation; ... study conducted in north India (n = 757)
judge.evidence_topic: Although the spread of misinformation is a pervasive and disruptive global problem, extant research is skewed towards “WEIRD” countries leaving questions about how to tackle misinformation in the developing world with different media and consumption patterns unanswered. We report the results of a game-based intervention against misinformation in India.
judge.reason: O artigo relata um ensaio controlado randomizado de um jogo de inoculação contra desinformação na Índia, sem foco em COVID-19, vacinas, eleições ou política partidária. Todos os dados extraídos estão corretos e consistentes com o resumo.

items.title: Long-term effectiveness of inoculation against misinformation: Three longitudinal experiments

judge.evidence_empirical: In 3 experiments (NExp1 = 151, NExp2 = 194, NExp3 = 170), participants played either Bad News (inoculation group) or Tetris (gamified control group) and rated the reliability of news headlines that either used a misinformation technique or not.
judge.evidence_topic: Using 3 longitudinal experiments (2 preregistered), we tested the effectiveness of Bad News, a real-world intervention in which participants develop resistance against misinformation.
judge.reason: O achado afirma estabilidade por pelo menos3 meses nos três experimentos, mas o resumo mostra que isso ocorreu apenas no Experimento1; no Experimento2 houve decaimento significativo, de forma que o efeito de longo prazo não era mais significativo. Portanto, o achado está parcialmente sustentado.

items.title: Winning the game against fake news? Using games to inoculate adolescents and young adults in Singapore against fake news

judge.evidence_empirical: aquellos que jugaron el juego mejoraron posteriormente en sus puntajes autoinformados sobre la percepción de noticias falsas como una amenaza, el escepticismo hacia la información de las redes sociales y la cautela sobre creer en la información que encuentran en línea. También encontramos que aquellos que jugaron el juego obtuvieron una puntuación más alta en la detección de noticias falsas que aquellos que no jugaron el juego
judge.evidence_topic: Winning the game against fake news? Using games to inoculate adolescents and young adults in Singapore against fake news
judge.reason: O artigo trata de um jogo digital de inoculação contra desinformação em Singapura, dentro do escopo. O resumo descreve um experimento com grupo de comparação e dados próprios, e o achado extraído é integralmente suportado pelo resumo.

items.title: Feedback exercises boost discernment of misinformation for gamified inoculation interventions

judge.evidence_empirical: two preregistered lab experiments (N1 = 191, N2 = 321) and four quasi-experimental in-game surveys implemented in Harmony Square (N3 = 559) and Bad News (N4 = 2,558, N5 = 419, N6 = 882)
judge.evidence_topic: Gamification is a promising approach to reducing misinformation susceptibility. Previous research has found that 'inoculation' games such as Bad News and Harmony Square help build cognitive resistance against misinformation.
judge.reason: O artigo trata de jogos de inoculação contra desinformação, é empírico com experimentos e quase-experimentos próprios, os métodos descritos batem com o resumo e o achado extraído é plenamente sustentado pelo trecho 'primarily by improving accuracy at detecting real news'.

items.title: Technique-based inoculation against real-world misinformation

judge.evidence_empirical: in two separate experiments (total n = 2188)
judge.evidence_topic: Inoculation theory has become an increasingly common framework for reducing susceptibility to both individual examples of misinformation (issue-based inoculation) and to the techniques and strategies that are commonly used to mislead or misinform people (technique-based inoculation).
judge.reason: O artigo trata de intervenção em forma de jogo digital (Bad News) contra desinformação, atende aos critérios de ser empírico e de método, e o achado extraído está inteiramente apoiado no resumo.

items.title: Good News about Bad News: Gamified Inoculation Boosts Confidence and Cognitive Immunity Against Fake News

judge.evidence_empirical: Using a 2 (treatment vs. control) × 2 (pre vs. post) mixed design (N = 196) we measure participants’ ability to spot misinformation techniques in 18 fake headlines before and after playing Bad News.
judge.evidence_topic: the Bad News game, an online fake news game in which players learn about six common misinformation techniques.
judge.reason: O artigo trata do jogo Bad News, que é um jogo de inoculação contra desinformação, dentro do recorte (jogo, sem tópicos excluídos). O estudo é empírico, com coleta de dados próprios em um experimento misto 2x2 (N=196). O método extraído coincide com o descrito no resumo. O achado de melhora na capacidade de identificar técnicas e aumento da confiança está integralmente apoiado no resumo, incluindo a ressalva sobre a direção correta.

items.title: How to “inoculate” against multimodal misinformation: A conceptual replication of Roozenbeek and van der Linden (2020)

judge.evidence_empirical: To test the game’s efficacy, we conducted a conceptual replication ( N = 380) of Roozenbeek and van der Linden’s 2020 study about Harmony Square, with the same study design, item set, and hypotheses.
judge.evidence_topic: Gamified “inoculation” interventions have shown promise in improving people’s ability to recognize manipulation techniques commonly used in misinformation… We developed a game called Cat Park, in which players learn about five manipulation techniques… and how misinformation can spread through images.
judge.reason: O artigo descreve um jogo de inóculo contra desinformação (Cat Park), testado em um experimento com dados próprios. O achado extráido é plenamente sustentado pelo resumo.

items.title: Playing an Augmented Reality Escape Game Promotes Learning About Fake News

judge.reason: O artigo aborda um jogo educacional (Escape Fake) para combate à desinformação, sem foco em COVID-19, vacinas, eleições ou política partidária. É um estudo empírico com dados próprios de um pré-teste/pós-teste, e o achado principal sobre o aumento do conhecimento e efeitos menores está claramente sustentado pelo resumo.

items.title: MAthE the Game: A Serious Game for Education and Training in News Verification

items.title: With Games Against Fake News – Developing Critical Thinking with the Help of the Card Game Follow Me

judge.evidence_empirical: This study aims to validate the contribution of the game Follow me in building resilience to fake news through an experiment on a sample of 130 secondary school students.
judge.evidence_topic: a game developed by Impact Games studio named Follow me, which is focused on developing critical thinking skills in the context of countering fake news.
judge.reason: O achado principal extraído é suportado pelo resumo: "although there was no global statistically significant improvement measured in students’ ability to recognize fake news, students are healthily skeptical of information", e o trecho ainda acrescenta que os estudantes rotulavam notícias como não confiáveis com maior frequência.

items.title: Inoculation against conspiracy theories: A consumer side approach to India's fake news problem

judge.evidence_empirical: We test the game's impact on an Indian sample (n = 1002) using a within‐subject design.
judge.evidence_topic: We attempt to replicate Roozenbeek and van der Linden's Western‐based study in India by employing the Bad News Game, an online game, in which players take on the role of a misinformation tycoon. They are exposed to weakened doses of the strategies employed in conspiracy and fake news production with the aim to cognitively inoculate them against misinformation.
judge.reason: O trecho do resumo relata melhora significativa na identificação de desinformação produzida com as técnicas de Conspiração, Personificação e, em menor grau, Descrédito, além de maior discernimento de notícias verdadeiras, o que confere suporte integral ao achado extrato.
